title_en: Interpretation (II) of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Book of Marriage and Family of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 Where a party requests confirmation of invalidity of a marriage due to bigamy under Article 1051(1) of the Civil Code, and at the time of prosecution the party to the lawful marriage has already divorced or the spouse has already died, and the defendant argues on this ground that the later marriage has become valid from the occurrence of the above circumstances, the People's Court shall not support such argument.

Article 2 After a couple has registered a divorce, if one party requests confirmation of invalidity of the divorce on the ground that the expression of intention of both parties was false, the People's Court shall not support such request.

Article 3 Where a creditor of one spouse has evidence proving that the property division clause in the divorce agreement affects the realization of its claim, and requests revocation of the relevant clause by reference to Article 538 or Article 539 of the Civil Code, the People's Court shall comprehensively consider the overall division and performance of the community property, the burden of child support, the fault in the divorce, and other factors, and shall support the request according to law.

Article 5 Before marriage or during the marital relationship, if the parties agree to transfer the ownership registration of a house owned by one party to the name of the other party or both parties, and at the time of divorce proceedings the ownership of the house has not yet been transferred and registered, and the parties dispute the ownership or division of the house and cannot reach an agreement through negotiation, the People's Court may, based on the claim of the party, taking into account the purpose of the gift, and comprehensively considering factors such as the duration of the marital relationship, the circumstances of cohabitation and having common children, fault in the divorce, the extent of contribution to the family, and the market price of the house at the time of divorce, render a judgment that the house belongs to one of the parties and determine whether the party who obtains the house shall compensate the other party and the specific amount of compensation.
Before marriage or during the marital relationship, if one party transfers the ownership registration of its own house to the name of the other party or both parties, and in divorce proceedings the parties dispute the ownership or division of the house and cannot reach an agreement through negotiation, if the duration of the marital relationship is relatively short and the giver has no serious fault, the People's Court may, based on the claim of the party, render a judgment that the house belongs to the giver, and, taking into account the purpose of the gift, comprehensively considering factors such as the circumstances of cohabitation and having common children, fault in the divorce, the extent of contribution to the family, and the market price of the house at the time of divorce, determine whether the party who obtains the house shall compensate the other party and the specific amount of compensation.
Where the giver has evidence proving that the other party has committed fraud, coercion, materially infringed upon the lawful rights and interests of the giver or his/her close relatives, or failed to perform support obligations owed to the giver, etc., and requests revocation of the civil juristic acts provided in the preceding two paragraphs, the People's Court shall support the request according to law.

Article 6 If one spouse, without the consent of the other spouse, uses community property to give tips on a live-streaming platform, and the amount obviously exceeds the general consumption level of the family, thereby seriously damaging the interests of the community property, it may be determined as "dissipation" as provided in Articles 1066 and 1092 of the Civil Code. If the other spouse requests division of the community property during the marital relationship, or requests that the tipping spouse receive a smaller share or no share at all when dividing the community property upon divorce, the People's Court shall support such request.

Article 7 If one spouse, for the purpose of bigamy, cohabiting with another person, or other violations of the duty of fidelity, donates community property to a third party or disposes of community property at a manifestly unreasonable price, and the other spouse claims that such civil juristic act is void as contrary to public order and good customs, the People's Court shall support such claim and shall handle the matter in accordance with Article 157 of the Civil Code.
Where one spouse falls under the circumstances specified in the preceding paragraph, and the other spouse, on the ground that the said spouse has transferred or sold community property, thereby seriously damaging the interests of the community property, requests division of the community property during the marital relationship pursuant to Article 1066 of the Civil Code, or requests that the said spouse receive a smaller share or no share at all when dividing the community property upon divorce pursuant to Article 1092 of the Civil Code, the People's Court shall support such request.

Article 8 During the marital relationship, if a house purchased by the couple is fully funded by one spouse's parent, and the gift contract expressly stipulates that it is given only to his/her own child, the matter shall be handled according to the contract; if there is no stipulation or the stipulation is unclear, when dividing the community property upon divorce, the People's Court may render a judgment that the house belongs to the child of the funding parent, and comprehensively consider factors such as the circumstances of cohabitation and having common children, fault in the divorce, the extent of contribution to the family, and the market price of the house at the time of divorce, to determine whether the party who obtains the house shall compensate the other party and the specific amount of compensation.
During the marital relationship, if a house purchased by the couple is partially funded by one spouse's parent or funded by both parents, and the gift contract expressly stipulates that the corresponding funding is given only to his/her own child, the matter shall be handled according to the contract; if there is no stipulation or the stipulation is unclear, when dividing the community property upon divorce, the People's Court may, based on the claim of the party and on the basis of the source and proportion of funding, comprehensively consider factors such as the circumstances of cohabitation and having common children, fault in the divorce, the extent of contribution to the family, and the market price of the house at the time of divorce, render a judgment that the house belongs to one of the parties, and the party who obtains the house shall give reasonable compensation to the other party.

Article 9 If one spouse transfers equity interests in a limited liability company that were subscribed for with community property but registered in his/her own name, and the other spouse requests confirmation that the equity transfer contract is void on the ground that it infringes upon the interests of the community property without his/her consent, the People's Court shall not support such request, unless there is evidence proving that the transferor and the transferee maliciously colluded to damage the lawful rights and interests of the other spouse.

Article 10 If a couple invests community property in a limited liability company and both are registered as shareholders, and the parties have no agreement or the agreement is unclear as to the ownership of the corresponding equity interests, upon divorce, if one party requests that the proportion of equity division be determined according to the respective capital contributions recorded in the register of shareholders or the company's articles of association, the People's Court shall not support such request; the People's Court shall handle the request of the parties to divide the community property in accordance with Article 1087 of the Civil Code.

Article 11 If one spouse claims that the waiver of inheritance by the other spouse is invalid on the ground that the property inheritable by the other spouse is community property and the waiver of inheritance infringes upon the interests of the community property, the People's Court shall not support such claim, unless there is evidence proving that the waiver of inheritance results in the waiving party being unable to perform the statutory support obligation.

Article 12 If one parent or his/her close relatives forcibly take away or hide a minor child, and the other parent applies to the People's Court for a personal safety protection order or, by reference to Article 997 of the Civil Code, applies for an injunction against infringement of personality rights, the People's Court shall support the application according to law.
If the party who forcibly took away or hid the minor child claims that its act of taking away or hiding was reasonably justified on the ground that the other parent engaged in gambling, drug abuse, domestic violence, or other serious infringements upon the lawful rights and interests of the minor child, the People's Court shall inform such party to resolve the issue through legal channels such as revocation of guardianship, suspension of visitation rights, or modification of the custodial relationship. If the party fails to provide evidence to prove the above claim and fails to file a relevant request within a reasonable period, the People's Court shall handle the matter in accordance with the preceding paragraph.

Article 13 During the period of separation between spouses, if one spouse or his/her close relatives forcibly take away or hide a minor child, causing the other spouse to be unable to perform guardianship duties, and the other spouse requests the actor to bear civil liability, the People's Court may, by reference to the relevant provisions of Article 1084 of the Civil Code concerning child care after divorce, temporarily determine the matters of child care for the minor child, and clarify that the party who temporarily directly cares for the minor child has the obligation to assist the other party in performing guardianship duties.

Article 15 If both parents, in their capacity as legal representatives, dispose of a house purchased with community property and registered in the name of the minor child, and later claim to the counterparty that such civil juristic act is void on the ground that it violates Article 35 of the Civil Code and damages the interests of the minor child, the People's Court shall not support such claim.

Article 16 An agreement in the divorce agreement that one party directly cares for a minor child or an adult child who cannot live independently, and the other party does not bear child support, is legally binding on both parties. However, after divorce, if the economic situation of the party directly caring for the child changes, resulting in a significant decline in the original standard of living, or if the necessary and reasonable expenses for the child's living, education, medical care, etc., have significantly increased, and the minor child or the adult child who cannot live independently requests the other party to pay child support, the People's Court shall support the request according to law, and shall determine the amount of child support by comprehensively considering the overall provisions of the divorce agreement, the actual needs of the child, the ability of the other party to bear, the local living standard, and other factors.
Under the circumstances specified in the proviso of the preceding paragraph, if the other party requests modification of the custodial relationship on the ground that the party directly caring for the child lacks the ability to care for the child, the People's Court shall handle the matter in accordance with Article 1084 of the Civil Code.

Article 17 After divorce, if the party who does not directly care for the child fails to pay child support in accordance with the divorce agreement or a commitment made in other ways, and the minor child or the adult child who cannot live independently requests payment of the overdue child support, the People's Court shall support such request.
Under the circumstances specified in the preceding paragraph, if the child has already reached adulthood and is able to live independently, and the party who directly cares for the child requests the other party to pay the overdue expenses, the People's Court shall support such request according to law.

Article 18 With respect to the fact that a stepchild has been raised and educated by a stepfather or stepmother under Article 1072 of the Civil Code, the People's Court shall determine it based on the length of common living, and comprehensively consider whether the stepparent actually provided daily care, performed the duty of family education, and bore child support expenses during the period of common living.

Article 19 After divorce between the biological father and stepmother or between the biological mother and stepfather, if a party claims that the rights and obligations between the stepfather or stepmother and the stepchild who was raised and educated by them shall no longer be governed by the provisions of the Civil Code on the relationship between parents and children, the People's Court shall support such claim, unless there is a legally established adoptive relationship between the stepfather or stepmother and the stepchild, or the stepchild still lives with the stepfather or stepmother.
After the dissolution of the step-relationship, if the stepfather or stepmother who lacks the ability to work and lacks a source of livelihood requests the adult stepchild who was once raised and educated by them to provide living expenses, the People's Court may, taking into comprehensive consideration factors such as the circumstances of raising and education and the ability of the adult stepchild to bear, support the request according to law, unless the stepfather or stepmother has previously abused or abandoned the stepchild or engaged in other similar conduct.

Article 20 If a divorce agreement provides that part or all of the community property shall be given to the child, after divorce, if one party requests revocation of such provision before the transfer of property rights, the People's Court shall not support such request, unless the other party consents.
If one party fails to perform the obligations stipulated in the divorce agreement of the preceding paragraph, and the other party requests that such party assume civil liability for continued performance or compensation for losses due to inability to perform, the People's Court shall support such request according to law.
If the parties expressly stipulate in the divorce agreement that the child may directly claim rights over the relevant property mentioned in paragraph 1 of this Article, and one party fails to perform the obligations stipulated in the divorce agreement, and the child requests, by reference to paragraph 2 of Article 522 of the Civil Code, that such party assume civil liability for continued performance or compensation for losses due to inability to perform, the People's Court shall support such request according to law.
If a divorce agreement provides that part or all of the community property shall be given to the child, after divorce, if one party has evidence proving that there was fraud, coercion, or other circumstances at the time of signing the divorce agreement, and requests revocation of such provision, the People's Court shall support such request according to law; if the party also requests division of that part of the community property, the People's Court shall handle the matter in accordance with Article 1087 of the Civil Code.

Article 21 In divorce proceedings, if one spouse has evidence proving that he/she bore more obligations during the marital relationship due to raising children, caring for the elderly, assisting the other spouse's work, etc., and requests compensation from the other spouse pursuant to Article 1088 of the Civil Code, the People's Court may determine the amount of compensation by comprehensively considering factors such as the time and energy invested in bearing the corresponding obligations, the impact on both parties, the ability of the paying party to bear, and the per capita disposable income of local residents.

Article 22 In divorce proceedings, if one party is in living difficulties due to old age, disability, serious illness, etc., and requests appropriate assistance from the other party who has the ability to bear pursuant to Article 1090 of the Civil Code, the People's Court may, based on the party's request and taking into account the property situation of the other party, support the request according to law.
Article 23 This Interpretation shall come into force as of February 1, 2025.
